_comment: Sitterwise payroll rules. Edit this file to change how payroll is calculated. Every payroll run records which version of this file it used, so reopening an old payroll shows the rules that were in force at the time.
effective_notes: Settled with Amy, 22 August 2026: California 8/40 overtime with double time; weekly overtime off (daily overtime already covers every real August pay week); pay tier inferred from the amount paid until Sitterwise records a children count; pay periods are Monday-to-Sunday weeks; mileage is Care.com only, paying the miles above 40 round trip.

pay_rates._comment: Hourly rates Sitterwise pays caregivers. 'label' is what Amy sees on screen.

minimum_booking._comment: Sitterwise guarantees caregivers a minimum number of paid hours per booking. The hours above what was actually worked are GUARANTEE PAY, not hours worked, so they are paid but do NOT count toward overtime thresholds.

overtime._comment: California overtime, 8/40 with double time. Amy's decision, 22 August 2026: Sitterwise caregivers are treated as ordinary non-exempt employees - time and a half over 8 hours in a day and 40 in a week, double time over 12, and seventh-consecutive-day rules. This is the conservative reading and the one that applies to Sitterwise. The alternative (personal attendants under the Domestic Worker Bill of Rights: 9/45, no double time) is not being used. Every threshold below is still a setting, so this can be revisited without touching any code.

weekly_overtime._comment: OFF by default per Amy's decision (daily overtime only). When off, the app still WARNS about anyone crossing the threshold so nothing is hidden.

seventh_consecutive_day._comment: On the 7th consecutive day worked in a workweek: first 8 hours at 1.5x, everything beyond at 2x.

overtime._workweek_note: Sitterwise payroll runs Monday through Sunday, weekly - confirmed from sitterwise.com/payroll-question. Pay stubs go out Tuesday, direct deposit lands Friday. Because the pay period IS the workweek, weekly overtime is straightforward here: there is no part-week to allocate.

bonuses._comment: Bonus and Lifesaver Bonus are taxable wages. If they are NON-discretionary, California law generally requires folding them into the regular rate, which raises overtime. The app does not do this automatically - it warns when a caregiver has both a bonus and overtime in the same week so Amy can decide.

tips._comment: California: tips belong to the employee and are excluded from the regular rate for overtime. They are taxable wages but are entered in OnPay as their own category.

reimbursements._comment: Business expense reimbursements under Labor Code 2802. Never taxable, never wages, never part of the regular rate.

mileage._comment: Mileage policy, from sitterwise.com/mileage-request. Care.com jobs only - not hotel jobs, not other private residence jobs. Only the miles ABOVE 40 round trip are paid: a 60-mile round trip pays 20 miles. Trips of 40-50 miles are submitted at check-out; anything over 50 miles must be approved in advance on the mileage request form.

rates_by_effective_date.source: IRS 2026 business standard mileage rate, Jan 1 - Jun 30
IRS 2026 business standard mileage rate, Jul 1 - Dec 31

mileage._eligibility_note: Set eligible_service_types to [] to allow mileage on any job. Empirically, all 7 mileage reimbursements in the August 2026 export were Corporate jobs and the smallest was exactly 40 miles.
mileage._amount_represents_note: What the Reimbursement figure in the export actually stands for. 'whole_trip' means the amount covers every mile driven; 'payable_miles' means the 40-mile deduction was already taken off before it was entered. Set to whole_trip because in the August 2026 export all seven mileage claims are over by exactly $30.40 - forty miles at $0.76 - and not one claim falls in the $0.76 to $7.60 range a correct 40-50 mile claim would produce.

payable_statuses._comment: Which Sitterwise booking statuses get paid. Amy's decision 2026-08-21: all completed jobs including Corporate and Group Childcare. 'confirmed' jobs are never paid, only flagged when they are past-dated.

service_types._comment: All service types are paid the same way. Listed here so the app can warn about anything it has not seen before.

pay_period._comment: How pay periods are shaped. Sitterwise pays weekly, Monday to Sunday. The app offers those weeks first when you upload an export, and half-months after them in case you ever need to run one.
